description: This module allows the administration of Keycloak realm using the Keycloak REST API. It requires access to the REST API using OpenID Connect; the user connecting and the realm being used must have the requisite access rights. In a default Keycloak installation, admin-cli and an admin user would work, as would a separate realm definition with the scope tailored to your needs and a user having the expected roles.

examples:
- name: Create or update Keycloak realm (minimal example)
  community.general.keycloak_realm:
    auth_client_id: admin-cli
    auth_keycloak_url: https://auth.example.com/auth
    auth_realm: master
    auth_username: USERNAME
    auth_password: PASSWORD
    realm: unique_realm_name
    state: present

- name: Delete a Keycloak realm
  community.general.keycloak_realm:
    auth_client_id: admin-cli
    auth_keycloak_url: https://auth.example.com/auth
    auth_realm: master
    auth_username: USERNAME
    auth_password: PASSWORD
    realm: unique_realm_name
    state: absent

return_values.name: end_state
return_values.description: Representation of realm after module execution (sample is truncated). Returned: on success Sample: {"adminUrl": "http://www.example.com/admin_url", "attributes": {"request.object.signature.alg": "RS256"}}

return_values.name: existing
return_values.description: Representation of existing realm (sample is truncated). Returned: always Sample: {"adminUrl": "http://www.example.com/admin_url", "attributes": {"request.object.signature.alg": "RS256"}}

return_values.name: msg
return_values.description: Message as to what action was taken. Returned: always Sample: "Realm testrealm has been updated"

return_values.name: proposed
return_values.description: Representation of proposed realm. Returned: always Sample: {"realm": "test"}
